newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER - BECKENBAUER BLASTS TV PROPOSALS FOR MORE ADVERTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - BECKENBAUER BLASTS TV PROPOSALS FOR MORE ADVERTS.

text.p: Bayern Munich president Franz Beckenbauer on Monday blasted proposals by televsion bosses to introduce more breaks for advertising into soccer matches.
Beckenbauer described the whole discussion as "as useful as a hole in the head" and "the nonsense of the century".
The former World Cup winning captain and coach was responding to suggestions from two of Germany's leading private broadcasters to divide games into thirds or bring in basketball-style time-outs.

"Soccer is all about speed and class," Beckenbauer wrote in Monday's edition of the Bild daily, using VfB Stuttgart's 5-0 demolition of Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday as an example of all that was good in the game.

"If Moenchengladbach had been able to call a time-out, the flow of the game would have been killed," Beckenbauer said. "Nobody wants to see that and that's why I think this whole discussion is the nonsense of the century."

Bosses at television stations RTL and Sat1 had warned in a Sunday newspaper that the high cost of soccer rights meant the game would soon be available only on pay-per-view TV unless they could pull in more advertising revenue.
